rule: A task is in the cross-language set when every function in its signature is a pure function over Int, Bool, String and lists of those (List[Int], List[List[Int]]), and its oracle is a list of assert_eq(call, literal) cases. Those types have one obvious spelling in every plugin language, so the prompt differs only in the language name and the rendered signature, and the oracle is the same cases rendered per language. The oracle is read from the task's own tests.almd (the file the Almide daily run scores against) and the signature from its prompt.md; the behavior text is msr/specs/<task>.md, the prompt's Behavior section with the Almide stdlib notes removed.

include.why: Int -> Int (largest case 10! fits in 32 bits)
two (String, Int) -> String functions; one case composes them
two String -> String functions; one case composes them
four functions over List[List[Int]] and List[Int]

exclude.why: returns Option[Int]: Option has a different spelling per language (Option, (int, bool), number | null, ?i64, Result/Option, Int?), and choosing one is a per-language difficulty decision
returns Map[String, Int]: no shared literal or equality across the plugin languages
takes a function argument and returns a tuple: the oracle needs lambda syntax per language
takes a function argument: the oracle needs lambda syntax per language
the signature is a user-defined ADT; declaring it is language-specific
user-defined ADT plus a function argument
Result[Int, String] returns: error encoding differs per language

Almide effect fn and budget semantics: no counterpart elsewhere
Almide effect fn and deadline semantics: no counterpart elsewhere
Almide effect fn and Result: no counterpart elsewhere
